questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following statements :
 1. Jhelum River passes through Wular Lake.
 2. Krishna River directly feeds Kolleru Lake.
 3. Meandering of Gandak River formed Kanwar 
 Lake.
 How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.questionTextHi:
[भारतीय भूगोल: UPSC IAS आधिकारिक प्रश्न • I.A.S. (Pre) 2023]
प्रश्न (हिंदी संस्करण): निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए :
 1. झेलम नदी से होकर गुजरती है वुलर झील.
 2. कृष्णा नदी directly feeds Kolleru झील.
 3. Meandering of गंडक नदी formed Kanwar 
 झील.
 How many of the statements given above are correct?
questions.explanationEn:
Wular's water main source is Jhelum river. There is a small 
island in the centre of this lake, called 'Zaina Lank'. It is 
worth mentioning that this island was constructed by King 
Zainul-Abi-Din. Hence statement 1 is correct.
While talking about second statement, Kolleru lake does 
not directly feed the Kolleru lake but the lake is fed by two 
other rivers namely Budameru and Tammileru. These two 
river is connected to the Krishna and Godawari Systems by 
inflowing drains and channels. Hence we can say that the 
Krishna River indirectly feeds the Kolleru lake through its 
tributaries. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.
The meandering of the Gandak river did not form the Kan-
war Lake, that is a freshwater oxbow lake located in Begus-
arai District of Bihar, India. Significantly the Kanwar Lake 
was formed by a cutoff meander of an old channel of Burhi 
Gandak River.
Hence statement 3 is not correct.

आधिकारिक उत्तर एवं व्याख्या (I.A.S. (Pre) 2023): सही विकल्प (A) है।
विस्तृत हिंदी विवरण:
Wular's water main source is Jhelum river. There is a small 
island in the centre of this lake, called 'Zaina Lank'. It is 
worth mentioning that this island was constructed by King 
Zainul-Abi-Din. Hence statement 1 is correct.
While talking about second statement, Kolleru lake does 
not directly feed the Kolleru lake but the lake is fed by two 
other rivers namely Budameru and Tammileru. These two 
river is connected to the Krishna and Godawari Systems by 
inflowing drains and channels. Hence we can say that the 
Krishna River indirectly feeds the Kolleru lake through its 
tributaries. Hence, statement 2 is not correct.
The meandering of the Gandak river did not form the Kan-
war Lake, that is a freshwater oxbow lake located in Begus-
arai District of Bihar, India. Significantly the Kanwar Lake 
was formed by a cutoff meander of an old channel of Burhi 
Gandak River.
Hence statement 3 is not correct.

questions.questionTextEn:

repeated falls in sea level, giving rise to present-day 
extensive marshland?
questions.questionTextHi:
[भारतीय भूगोल: UPSC IAS आधिकारिक प्रश्न • I.A.S. (Pre) 2023]

repeated falls in sea level, giving rise to present-day 
extensive marshland?
questions.explanationEn:
The Runn of Kutch is a Salt Marshy land. It is located in the 
Thar desert in the Kachchh district of Western Gujarat, India. 
This area was a once a sprawling shallow of the Arabian sea 
until a constant geological shift closed off the connection 
with the sea. Over the years, the region gradually became a 
seasonal marshy salt desert. The present day shoreline and 
the sand dune deposition of Kutch's is the result of hundreds 
of years of rainless years around 5,000 years ago.

questions.questionTextEn:
Consider the following statements:
 1. In India, the Himalayas are spread over fi ve States 
only.
 2. Western Ghats are spread over fi ve States only.
 3. Pulicat Lake is spread over two states only.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi:
[भारतीय भूगोल: UPSC IAS आधिकारिक प्रश्न • I.A.S. (Pre) 2017]
प्रश्न (हिंदी संस्करण): निम्नलिखित कथनों पर विचार कीजिए:
 1. In भारत, the हिमालय are spread over fi ve States 
only.
 2. पश्चिमी घाट are spread over fi ve States only.
 3. पुलिकट झील is spread over two states only.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanationEn:
The Himalayas are spread over most of the northern and 
north-eastern States & UTs i.e., Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, 
Himachal Pradesh, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, Arunachal Pradesh, 
Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. 
Besides these, mountain range of Assam and West Bengal 
are also part of the Himalayas. So, Himalayas are spread over 
more than five states. The Western Ghats are spread over the 
states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, Tamil Nadu 
and Kerala i.e., 6 states. Pulicat lake is second largest (after 
Chilika lake) lagoon in India, straddles the border of Tamil 
Nadu and Andhra Pradesh. Therefore statements 1 and 2 are 
wrong and statement 3 is correct.
questions.explanationHi:
आधिकारिक उत्तर एवं व्याख्या (I.A.S. (Pre) 2017): सही विकल्प (B) है।
विस्तृत हिंदी विवरण:
The Himalayas are spread over most of the northern and 
north-eastern States & UTs i.e., Jammu & Kashmir, Ladakh, 
हिमाचल प्रदेश, Uttarakhand, Sikkim, अरुणाचल प्रदेश, 
Meghalaya, Nagaland, Manipur, Mizoram and Tripura. 
Besides these, mountain range of Assam and पश्चिम बंगाल 
are also part of the Himalayas. So, Himalayas are spread over 
more than five states. The पश्चिमी घाट are spread over the 
states of Gujarat, Maharashtra, Goa, Karnataka, तमिलनाडु 
and Kerala i.e., 6 states. Pulicat lake is second largest (after 
Chilika lake) lagoon in India, straddles the border of Tamil 
Nadu and आंध्र प्रदेश. Therefore statements 1 and 2 are 
wrong and statement 3 is correct.

questions.questionTextEn:
With reference to river Teesta, consider the following 
statements :
 1. The source of river Teesta is the same as that of 
 Brahmaputra but it fl ows through Sikkim.
 2. River Rangeet originates in Sikkim and it is a 
 tributary of river Teesta.
 3. River Teesta fl ows into Bay of Bengal on the border 
 of India and Bangladesh.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.questionTextHi:
[भारतीय भूगोल: UPSC IAS आधिकारिक प्रश्न • I.A.S. (Pre) 2017]
प्रश्न (हिंदी संस्करण): के संदर्भ में नदी Teesta, consider the following 
statements :
 1. The source of नदी Teesta is the same as that of 
 ब्रह्मपुत्र but it fl ows through सिक्किम.
 2. नदी Rangeet originates in सिक्किम and it is a 
 की सहायक नदी नदी Teesta.
 3. नदी Teesta fl ows into बंगाल की खाड़ी on the border 
 of भारत and बांग्लादेश.
 Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
questions.explanationEn:
Teesta River originates from the Khangchung Chho glacial 
lake in Sikkim as Chhonbo Chhu river at an altitudes of approx. 
5280 meters. The source of the Brahmaputra River is the Angsi 
Glaciar in Tibet. Thus statement (1) is wrong.
River Rangeet originates in Sikkim and it is a tributary of 
river Teesta. Thus statement (2) is correct. Teesta river is a 
Tributary of Brahmaputra. Teesta River flows through Sik-
kim and West Bengal in India. It Joins Brahmaputra in Ban-
gladesh and falls into the Bay of Bengal. Thus statement (3) 
is wrong. Hence option (b) is correct answer.
questions.explanationHi:
आधिकारिक उत्तर एवं व्याख्या (I.A.S. (Pre) 2017): सही विकल्प (B) है।
विस्तृत हिंदी विवरण:
Teesta River का उद्गम होता है the Khangchung Chho glacial 
lake in Sikkim as Chhonbo Chhu river at an altitudes of approx. 
5280 meters. The source of the Brahmaputra River is the Angsi 
Glaciar in Tibet. Thus statement (1) is wrong.
River Rangeet originates in Sikkim and it is a की सहायक नदी 
river Teesta. Thus statement (2) is correct. Teesta river is a 
की सहायक नदी Brahmaputra. Teesta River flows through Sik-
kim and पश्चिम बंगाल in India. It Joins Brahmaputra in Ban-
gladesh and falls into the बंगाल की खाड़ी. Thus statement (3) 
is wrong. Hence option (b) is correct answer.

all the statements are correct.
